newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai forex control creates two dlr/baht markets.
newsitem.headline: Thai forex control creates two dlr/baht markets.

text.p: Thailand's decision to forbid commercial banks from offering short-term baht funds to foreign buyers since last week has created different dollar/baht rates for offshore and onshore markets, dealers said on Wednesday.

They said the Bank of Thailand's instruction for Thai-based banks not to quote dollar/baht swap rates to foreign buyers has sharply tightened baht supply in offshore markets where the Thai currency was traded substantially higher against the dollar than the central bank's midrate on Wednesday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed its dollar/baht midrate at 25.71 on Wednesday.
In offshore markets, the baht was quoted at about 25.100/25.125 in late morning against about 25.730/25.770 in the local market where no transaction restriction was imposed.
The Thai central bank on Friday banned the sale of baht in short-term forward and swap transactions by domestic banks to foreign clients.
The move cut off access to baht financing for currency speculators to cover their short baht positions which they used earlier for their attack on the Thai currency last week.
Dealers said they expect the wide gap between the local and foreign dollar/baht rates to stay as long as the central bank maintains its ban.
